meaning: Table cell text in the shared summary panel is drawn at 20 pt instead of the earlier 22 pt, because cells now carry a percentage in brackets and the wider string collided with the row label in the baseline column. It is a layout claim about string width, not a numerical result.

could_move.what: Font size of every data cell in this table panel, including the highlighted-window cell drawn in steelblue
Header/label column alignment, which is set at 11 pt against the values and assumes the label column ends where the first data column starts
Any deck rendering this panel, e.g. the jugular-compression comparison decks, where cell strings differ in length per patient

expectation: Cosmetic only if the claim holds: cells ~10% smaller, less chance of overlap with row labels. But whether 20 pt actually clears the label depends on the longest cell string produced by each deck, and I cannot tell that from this context. No effect on solver output or fitted numbers.

check.why: Replots one deck that reaches this panel without re-fitting, so you can look at whether the 20 pt cells and the 11 pt labels still clear each other.
